title: `repo grant list` of a mirror picks a placement without checking the active credentials can reach it

verdict.rationale: The evidence covers related auth and core-resolution code, but none of it addresses how a mirror placement is picked or whether the picked cluster is reachable by the active credentials. The commit that removed implicit login selection chose that the active context is the identity. It never decided that placement selection should ignore reachability, so the lexical pick looks like an unconsidered gap.

dials (mirror list, auth status)

The `mirror list` stderr banner re-derived its core via
ResolveControlPlaneTarget, which ignores ENTIRE_TOKEN. In env-token mode
the request instead dials the token's own aud, so with both ENTIRE_TOKEN
and a contexts.json present the banner named a core the request never
talks to. The precedence (env-token-then-active-context) lives only inside
coreapi.New, and the client hid its resolved core, so every "talking to X"
display site was forced to re-derive it and could get it wrong.

Add coreapi.Client.CoreOrigin() — the single source of truth for "which
core am I dialing", reporting whatever was wired in (active context,
NewForCluster's cluster core, or the ENTIRE_TOKEN aud). Render the mirror
list banner from the live client's CoreOrigin so it can never diverge from
the request; this also makes it correct (rather than suppressed) in
env-token mode.

Fix `entire auth status` the same way: it builds its own /me client outside
coreapi, so it now applies the env-token-first precedence and reports the
env token's core + bearer instead of a stale active context. logout stays
on the active context: it manages a stored session, which an env token lacks.

Extract auth.ParseEnvToken as the single owner of the ENTIRE_TOKEN
trim/blank/aud-validation sequence, shared by coreapi.New's bypass and
auth status (was duplicated inline in both).

Document the convention in CLAUDE.md: to show which core, ask the client
(CoreOrigin); never re-resolve for display.

refactor(auth): require the active context, dropping implicit login selection

Account selection had three tiers: the active context when the resource
trusted its core, else "the sole eligible context", else an ambiguity
error. The two implicit tiers are removed — the active context is the
identity, or the command fails.

The tiers made the acting identity depend on what *else* happened to be
stored. Adding a second login could silently change which account an
existing command ran as, and the same command could act as different
identities on two machines. Concretely: log into prod as alice, add a
staging login as admin for one task, and `git push` to a staging-fronted
cluster would authenticate as admin — an elevated account, with the
server-side audit trail recording it, and nothing in the output saying
so. For "whose credentials is this running under?", a predictable error
beats a convenient guess.

Multiple saved logins remain fully supported; `auth contexts`, `auth use`,
and `logout --all-contexts` are unchanged. What changes is that switching
is explicit.

Because "not logged in" is actively misleading for someone who IS logged
in, just to another federation, the failure now distinguishes what the
user can do about it: name the saved logins that would work and point at
`auth use`, or name the servers the resource trusts and point at
`entire login --server <url>`. That cashes in renderLoginHint's dead
